title: AI maps ledger and trial-balance data to tax accounts, with tie-out checks
problem: Ledger data from many entities and countries must be extracted, mapped to tax accounts and checked before a return is prepared, and a misclassified figure can flow through unflagged.
approach: EY describes a GenAI tool that standardises ledger data and maps it with pre-vetted prompts; Thomson Reuters aims for agentic mapping.
EY says the multi-country mapping step can become a two-day process in place of weeks (vendor-published; no client named).
A qualified team member reviews the mapping before loading, and the preparer ties a sample of figures to source documents.

title: Agents read K-1 footnotes, map tax treatments and learn from logged overrides
problem: Data arrives from several systems in different formats, and K-1 footnotes needed trained staff, heavy human review and group discussion when a footnote was unfamiliar.
approach: PwC says agents assess a footnote, state how they interpreted it and give a confidence level, working within its Agent OS.
PwC's AI tax leader says one person now reviews where three might have gathered; no figures published (self-reported).
The reviewer checks flagged items, and every override carries a recorded reason the agent learns from.

title: AI compares returns and source data year on year, flagging anomalies
problem: Reviewers of corporate returns compare against prior years and source schedules by hand, while tax authorities increasingly use real-time analytics to find errors.
approach: EY says AI-enabled comparison can pinpoint inconsistencies; Baker Tilly describes AI flagging unusual effective tax rate movements across entities.
Deloitte cites agents flagging anomalies in source data and reconciliations for human review; Corptax lists PDF comparison on its roadmap.
The reviewer decides which flagged items matter, and the preparer resolves each before sign-off. No outcome figures are published.

title: Validation agents critique other agents' output; reviewers do first-level review
problem: Reviewers face rising volumes of work in which errors are quiet and technical, and now receive conclusions to review rather than subtotals to check.
approach: A Thomson Reuters Institute recap says some seminar attendees use validation agents to critique their own agents' outputs.
OpenAI's 2026 job listing includes first-level review and validation of automated provision outputs. No outcome figures are published.
A named reviewer signs off the compliance output and samples both AI-flagged and unflagged items.

title: Preparation shifts to AI and staff review it, with fewer review layers
problem: Today a staff-level team member does most compliance preparation, followed by layers of review.
approach: EY says AI will in future do much of the preparation while staff monitor it, and fewer review levels may be needed.
PwC says complex outputs such as tax calculations keep multi-eye review, while simple diagnostics may not need three layers.
A qualified professional reviews AI-prepared output. No outcome figures are published.

title: Agents roll forward prior-year workpapers and prepare review-ready business returns
problem: Business-return preparation involves inconsistent client data and review-heavy processes, and most CPA automation had focused on personal returns because business returns were too complex.
approach: Byron says agents roll prior-year workpapers into a current-year workbook, request missing information and produce source-linked, confidence-scored output.
Byron says its extraction is more than 97% accurate (vendor-published); Thomson Reuters and RSM describe similar plans.
Accountants verify outputs and a professional gives final review before filing.

title: In-house tax team moves from outsourced preparation to agent-driven return computation
problem: A company sending its income, gross receipts and property tax compliance to outside preparers must manage vendors, reconcile provision to return and track deadlines through spreadsheets and email.
approach: OpenAI's tax team listed a 2025 role to move to internal, agent-powered return computation on version-controlled tax-logic libraries, with a Corptax implementation.
OpenAI tax staff demonstrated live automation pipelines in 2026; a 2025 listing states a 12-month goal to automate the tax stack (self-reported).
A manager oversees vendors during the transition, and reviewers perform first-level review of automated outputs.

title: Large firms build agent platforms to create and manage tax agents
problem: Firms and clients need many agents for data collection and compliance tasks, and dozens of unmanaged agents lack performance tracking and coordination.
approach: EY describes a Tax Agent Factory to build and manage agents at scale; KPMG and Anthropic put Claude inside KPMG's client platform.
EY said in March 2025 it planned as many as 150 agents for 80,000 tax professionals (self-reported); no usage data published.
Human review of agent outputs continues inside client engagements, with firm-level governance committee oversight at PwC.

title: AI builds R&D credit evidence from project, payroll and ledger systems
problem: Form 6765 Section G, a business-component breakdown of research expenses, becomes required for tax years after 2025, and interview-based after-the-fact studies struggle to meet that standard.
approach: Thomson Reuters says Neo.Tax links project, payroll and ERP systems, groups tickets into components, applies the four-part test and populates Form 6765.
Thomson Reuters says filing time falls from weeks to days and companies report 50-75% savings versus accounting-firm fees (vendor-published).
An R&D tax lead confirms each component qualifies; project owners confirm data; the preparer reviews Section G narratives and cost allocation.

title: In-house tax team uses a governed AI platform for data reconciliation
problem: Vendor Kognitos argues the binding constraint in corporate tax is now assembling and reconciling source data from ledgers and systems, not the calculation itself.
approach: Savant says its platform turns messy data into governed outputs with an audit trail, and planned a 2026 session with Oxford Industries.
Savant's demonstrations covered multi-system reconciliation, document extraction and reporting with lineage; no outcome figures are published for Oxford (vendor-published).
Tax staff review reconciliation exceptions, and a data owner approves write-backs or reviews a log of them.

title: Cited AI tax research inside compliance tools, with every authority verified
problem: Compliance staff leave their return or workpaper tool to research positions, and general chatbots can invent authorities, creating a professional-conduct risk.
approach: Thomson Reuters embedded CoCounsel Tax in ONESOURCE in late 2024; Bloomberg Tax added AI insights to Workpapers and Compliance Tracker.
Thomson Reuters says junior staff can handle more complex questions with cited sources; no figure is published (vendor-published).
The preparer reads each cited authority before relying on it, and a reviewer cross-checks authorities in supporting memos.

title: Agents track filing calendars and rule changes, reporting to the tax team
problem: Corporate departments track due dates, extensions and rule changes across many entities, often in spreadsheets, while forms and instructions change frequently.
approach: Bloomberg Tax announced an AI Assistant in its Compliance Tracker; Orbitax's XatBot tracks regulatory changes and sends comparison reports.
Bloomberg Tax says the assistant saves time and reduces risk, without a measurement (vendor-published).
A tax technical lead decides which changes affect returns or payments, and a person approves any filing or payment action.

title: Pre-filing audit-risk prediction and anomaly screening of the return
problem: The IRS already uses machine learning to score corporate returns line by line, but preparers get no equivalent signal before filing.
approach: Corptax lists audit prediction to address potential triggers early on its AI roadmap; no outcome figures are published (vendor-published).
Deloitte's framework says low company AI adoption against a high-adoption tax authority brings heightened audit and dispute exposure.
The reviewer decides whether a flag is an error, a reportable position or a documentation gap; tax decides whether to change course.

title: Continuously updated effective-tax-rate and cash-tax modelling with what-if scenarios
problem: Static spreadsheet models are slow to update when entity structure, transfer pricing or supply chains change, so the effect on cash taxes is seen late.
approach: Baker Tilly describes AI engines that ingest financial data and entity structures to calculate effective rates continuously and run what-if scenarios.
It also describes agents that download ERP trial balances, summarise them and compare to prior calculations; no figures published (vendor-published).
Tax reviews scenario outputs before decisions are made.

title: Compliance bought as an AI-enabled managed service, with AI use disclosed
problem: Corporate tax departments outsource return work, and 77% want providers to use GenAI while 59% are not sure whether their own companies do (vendor-published).
approach: Deloitte says some companies look to outsourcing to gain AI-powered solutions without capital outlay and upgrade costs.
The IRS Office of Professional Responsibility says practitioners should disclose AI activities; in-house teams can ask providers what AI is used.
Client and provider agree what AI does and who reviews it, and the tax director reviews disclosures at renewal.

title: Idea: value-based or fixed-fee pricing for AI-enabled compliance work
problem: This is an idea: AI cuts preparation time, and IRS guidance says billing for manual time not spent, or double billing AI-assisted tasks, may breach the fee rule.
approach: Bloomberg Tax reports top firms exploring value- and outcome-based fees as AI cuts billable hours.
The AICPA is seeking IRS clarification, saying the guidance does not appear to allow value pricing and overlooks software and governance costs.
An RSM partner illustrated a 20-hour advisory report taking 10 hours with AI (self-reported); the engagement partner sets the fee basis.

title: Tax analysts build own pipelines and agents with low-code and AI tools
problem: Data-integration pipelines would otherwise sit in an IT queue for about two months, and only half of corporate tax departments provided technology training in 2025.
approach: Seminar attendees described prompting AI tools to build data pipelines in about 15 minutes instead of a two-month IT queue (self-reported).
Orbitax's Autopilot is a conversational workflow builder inside its international tax platform.
Any pipeline is independently reviewed and documented before it feeds a return, and each automation has a named owner.

title: A tax model explains its inputs and assumptions; approved logic is locked
problem: CFOs ask whether AI-prepared tax work will hold up under IRS scrutiny; PwC says explainability, traceability and auditability are the test.
approach: PwC says a model it uses for effective tax rates explains inputs, output and assumptions, so the logic chain replaces a memo.
Once approved, logic is locked and people suggest improvements instead of making ad hoc changes; no figures are published (self-reported).
Tax calculation outputs keep multi-eye human review, and an approval step precedes locking.

title: Keep a record of AI use and verification with each AI-assisted item
problem: If no record shows what an AI tool did and what a person checked, the team cannot show the process behind an output when it is later challenged.
approach: Wolters Kluwer advises recording the prompt, output, citations, validation steps and conclusion; Thomson Reuters CoCounsel Tax returns cited sources and reasoning.
The IRS Office of Professional Responsibility lists documenting AI use and verification as a best practice. No outcome is published.
The preparer records what was verified and signs off; the reviewer confirms the record exists before sign-off.
who: Wolters Kluwer, Thomson Reuters, IRS OPR

title: Approved enterprise AI tools, vendor contract terms and revalidation after model changes
problem: Preparers use public AI tools with return data, risking exposure under disclosure law, and silent vendor model changes can alter outputs without triggering review.
approach: The IRS Office of Professional Responsibility says practitioners must use only secure, enterprise-approved AI for client data.
An AICPA framework lists contract terms: accuracy service level with remedy, 60 days' notice of material model changes, audit rights, error notice.
The tax director approves the tool list, and tax technology staff revalidate outputs after each notified vendor change.
who: IRS OPR, AICPA, KPMG Germany survey

title: Gated rollout of AI-drafted return work with logging, thresholds and unaided-competence checks
problem: Faster AI preparation can make review less rigorous in practice, few teams measure what AI does, and juniors who never draft may not learn to review.
approach: An AICPA framework phases adoption from research and summarisation to AI-drafted positions, each gated by full logging, override-rate review and error thresholds.
Thomson Reuters suggests tracking baselines for cycle time, documentation hours and audit exposure; one survey found only 20% measure GenAI return (vendor-published).
The signing preparer verifies every AI-drafted position; novel positions escalate to senior review; managers run an annual unaided-capability check.

title: Idea: deterministic engine computes the return; language model writes checked rule logic
problem: This is an idea: language models asked to compute a return directly do so unreliably, and returns must be computed exactly while rules keep changing.
approach: Researchers propose using the model to translate statutes and forms into executable logic checked against test returns, with a deterministic engine computing.
One such system matched all 51 held-out benchmark returns against 66% for the strongest language model alone (independent research).
Tax technology staff review generated logic and test coverage; the preparer reviews the computed return and flagged exceptions.

title: Idea: an input-check gate holds contradictory cases for a person before computing
problem: This is an idea: real inputs are often incomplete or contradictory, and a model computing straight through a contradiction returns a confident number with no warning.
approach: Researchers add one extra model call that checks the input for conflicts before computing, and abstain when it finds one.
In tests, strong models computed through injected contradictions without signalling the conflict in 63% to 76% of cases (independent research).
A person resolves every case where the gate abstains.

title: Idea: always-on compliance monitoring replaces periodic batch preparation
problem: This is an idea: compliance is prepared in periodic batches so issues surface at deadlines, while some authorities already see transactions as they happen.
approach: EY practitioners describe AI agents that analyse compliance metrics continuously and trigger alerts or remediation before deadlines.
Deloitte's fourth scenario envisions near real-time compliance with preventive AI-driven controls. No outcome figures are published.
A person reviews alerts and decides on remediation.
